Calculate Grade Computes the grade between two levels over a chainage and places it as a labelled percentage.

Run CALCGRADE . For each grade: Select first level or press Enter to input manually: — pick a level text and the number is read out of it, or press Enter to type a value. The same for the second level. Choose chainage method [Direct/Calculate]: — Direct to type the chainage, or Calculate to enter two lengths and use the difference. Specify point to place <grade> grade text: — the computed value is already shown in the prompt. It loops so you can do several in a row; Esc finishes.

The grade as a percentage to one decimal place, placed as WAE label text — for example 1.5% . The calculation is the level difference divided by the chainage. Note — a chainage of zero is rejected and the command starts again rather than failing. Previous Horizontal & Vertical Text Next Add Comment
Import Sheet Turns a folder of scanned or exported design sheets into one layout each, with the image stretched to the paper and the page set up ready to plot.

Run IMPORTSHEET . Specify sheet size [A4/A3/A2/A1] <A1>: — press Enter for A1. Pick the images in the file dialog. You can select many at once. It opens in the drawing's Rasters folder if there is one. If some sheets already have layouts you'll be asked once: N of the selected sheet(s) already have layouts [Replace/Skip] <Skip>: .

One layout per image, named after the file, with the image stretched to fill the sheet on the SHEET layer. Each layout is set up to plot as a PDF at the size you chose, rotated to landscape and centred using the BW plot styles, and opens framed on its sheet. Tip — the whole import is a single undo step. If it isn't what you wanted, one U removes every layout it made.

Sheets import but aren't set up to plot — the BW plot device isn't installed. Re-run the suite installer with the WAE component ticked. A file is skipped — its name couldn't be used as a layout name, or a layout with that name already exists and you chose Skip. Both are reported per file. Previous Works-As-Executed Next Preset Labels

Modify & Flip Text Two small tools for tidying annotation on a marked-up sheet.
Adds a prefix or suffix to selected text. Run MODTEXT — select the text first if you like — then Choose [Prefix/Suffix]: and Enter text for Prefix/Suffix: . Works on text, mtext and multileaders.

FLIPTEXT rotates selected text 180° about its middle centre — select the text first if you like. Useful when a marked-up sheet is rotated and annotation ends up upside down. Works on text and mtext. Note — flipping changes the text's justification to middle centre permanently, so flipping twice doesn't restore the original justification. Previous Add Comment Next Office Tools
Horizontal & Vertical Text Quick WAE text at a fixed rotation, for annotating rotated sheets without fighting the UCS.
HTXT — horizontal text at 0°. VTXT — vertical text at 270°.
Run the command, then Text insertion point: . Type the text in place and finish as normal. Because the WAE label style has a fixed height you're not asked for one.

MText on the ANNOTATIONS layer (colour 10) in the WAE LABEL style — Lucida Sans Unicode at a fixed 2.5 mm. The style is not annotative , unlike the drafting and engineering text commands. WAE plans are worked at paper scale, so the height is fixed rather than following the drawing's annotation scale. Layer and style are created on demand if they're missing. NSW Cadastral Lot Loader Pulls lot boundaries, labels and road names straight from NSW Spatial into model space — by lot and plan number, by a point, or by an extent.
Run NSWLOTS , or use the button on the WSY Tools ribbon tab. The panel stays open while you work. The ? button in its title bar opens offline help.

These control what gets labelled and whether road data comes in: Option Effect Subject Lot Labels Labels the lots you asked for (the By Lot ID search only). Adjoining Lot Labels Labels neighbouring lots. Adjacent only labels just those sharing a boundary; All also labels the surrounding buffer. On the By Point and By Extent searches this labels everything returned. Road Names Places road name text along each centreline. Road Centrelines Also draws the centreline geometry.

By Lot ID Enter the plan number (required) and optionally the lot and section, choosing DP or SP. Add more rows with + for multiple lots (up to ten), then click Fetch Lots . The Buffer is how far around each lot to fetch surrounding lots — set 0 for adjoining only (up to 5000 m). If an entry matches nothing, it's flagged on the command line so you can check the lot and plan. By Point Click Pick Point , pick in the drawing, set the buffer radius, then Fetch Lots — every lot within that radius is fetched. By Extent Choose Current View or Draw Rectangle , then Fetch Lots .

Layer Contents SUB BDY Subject lot boundaries SUB DP Subject lot labels ADJ BDY Adjoining and surrounding boundaries ADJ DP Adjoining labels ROAD NAME Road name text, rotated along the centreline ROAD CL Road centrelines The By Lot ID search separates the lots you asked for (SUB layers) from their neighbours (ADJ layers); the By Point and By Extent searches load everything onto the ADJ layers. Re-running never doubles up — lots already loaded are skipped. Your entries and settings are remembered for next time.

NSWLABELLOTS labels lots that were loaded earlier — select the boundaries and it reads the plan details stored on them. Watch out — it doesn't check whether a lot is already labelled. Running it twice over the same selection stacks a second set of labels on top of the first, which is easy to miss on screen. Undo rather than trying to pick the duplicates out. Watch out — the tool works out the MGA zone from the data it fetches. If it can't determine the zone it assumes Zone 56 and says so in the status bar. On a Zone 55 job that warning matters, so check the result lands where you expect.

The tool needs internet access to the NSW Spatial service. Transient errors are retried automatically; a persistent failure is reported in the status bar. Large extents can take a while — the Cancel button stops a fetch cleanly. Previous Office Tools Next Point Cloud Digitizer
Point Cloud Digitizer Traces features off a point cloud — step along at a fixed distance per vertex, or trace freely — with each vertex snapped to the cloud, numbered and coded as you go.
Run PCDIG , or use the button on the WSY Tools ribbon tab. Each drawing gets its own panel. The ? button in its title bar opens offline help.

Setting What it does Fixed-distance stepping The checkbox beside Segment Dist . With it on, each new vertex lands exactly the segment distance from the last in the direction you pick, and a guide circle shows that distance. Turn it off to trace freely — you click each vertex where you like and the distance field greys out. Segment distance How far each new vertex lands from the last while stepping. Read live — change it mid-string and the next segment uses the new value. Enable point creation Places a survey point at each vertex as well as the line. Uses Civil points where available (the label reads Civil or Standard to show which). Start number The first point number. Auto-fills past anything already used; the ↻ button finds the lowest free number. Point code The feature code written onto the points and string. Layer Set manually, or automatically from the code library.

Browse to a Trimble .fxl feature library with the … button. Once loaded, the point code becomes a searchable picker, and the layer and colour come from the selected feature automatically. The ✕ button unloads it. Note — the library isn't remembered between sessions; browse to it again when you reopen the drawing.

Add Line — pick a start point, then pick a direction for each following point. A guide circle shows the fixed distance. Undo steps back a point; Esc finishes the string. Add Point — places standalone points without a line. Undo steps back; Esc finishes. Extend — select an existing 3D polyline near the end you want to continue from. While digitising, ordinary 2D snaps are turned off and point-cloud snapping is turned on, then restored when you finish.

Export to 12da… writes every digitised string and point to a 12d Model ASCII file. Points sitting on a string vertex aren't duplicated. Colours come from the code library where one is loaded. Note — the export scans model space only, and can't run while a digitising run is active. Previous NSW Lot Loader Next Engineering
